sideEffects.via: NMDA blockade on prefrontal GABA interneurons → glutamate and dopamine excess

pearls: Reserved for patients with **multiple failures** of monoamine drugs, whereas 5HT/dopamine blockers are added after only one or two failures.
Works in apparently **nonmonoaminergic** depression; onset is almost immediate (minutes to hours), sometimes with a direct **anti-suicidal** effect.
Psychosis-like syndrome is mainly a feature of **high, acute** doses; slow **subanesthetic** infusions for depression are not thought to cause it.
Also raises **BDNF and VEGF**, so it may reverse synaptic atrophy within minutes, unlike monoamine drugs, whose growth-factor effect takes weeks.
The exact **R versus S** pharmacology, and that of their active metabolites, is still being worked out, though esketamine is clearly active as a rapid antidepressant.
It is unclear which **NMDA subtypes** it engages and what role its σ1, SERT and μ-opioid binding play in the rapid antidepressant effect.
**Deuteration** lengthens half-life and so changes the **quinidine dose** needed in the deuterated combination.
Used here only as a **2D6 booster**; the dose is kept below that with cardiovascular actions, and is adjusted when paired with deuterated dextromethorphan.
**Bupropion** is the alternative booster in the other combination, adding its own NDRI antidepressant action.
Racemic **methadone** is an oral μ-agonist for opioid use disorder; the opioid activity sits mostly in the **levo** form.
Whether NMDA block alone, the **NMDA subtype**, or accompanying μ, σ1 and SERT actions matter most is still unresolved, as for other NMDA antagonists.
Binds the **same sites** as general anesthetics (propofol, etomidate, alphaxolone, alfadalone), which are dosed far higher.
**Benzodiazepines lack antidepressant action**, so the **benzodiazepine-insensitive** (extrasynaptic) receptors are thought to be the key target.
Made and released by **glia** and captured by extrasynaptic δ-containing receptors; may also have **anxiolytic** potential.
How neurosteroids produce a rapid and possibly **lasting** antidepressant effect is unknown; reduced GABA in depression is one hint.
